title: Hodgkin Lymphoma
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) - physician decides. Pathway branches by histology (classical HL vs NLPHL vs pediatric/adolescent vs relapsed), then workup -> Ann Arbor staging and favorable/unfavorable or IPS risk -> stage/regimen-directed treatment (ABVD vs BV-AVD vs escalated BEACOPP) with interim-PET (Deauville) response adaptation -> surveillance -> relapsed/refractory salvage and transplant/cellular pathways. Treatment leaves show checklist guidance without invented doses; only pediatric leaves reference an existing StewardMD Standard Protocol. Structural content is standard oncology; no proprietary guideline text reproduced. DRAFT - not clinically activated.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with standard oncology references (NCCN / DeVita / Harrison), Hodgkin Lymphoma. Pediatric regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols; the dose engine computes patient doses.

a.text: Interim FDG-PET after 2 cycles is scored on the 5-point Deauville scale; Deauville 1-3 is treated as a negative (good) metabolic response and Deauville 4-5 as positive (inadequate) response.

b.text: Bleomycin carries a risk of cumulative pulmonary toxicity; response-adapted omission after a negative interim PET reduces lung exposure without loss of disease control in the settings where it has been studied.

c.text: Discuss fertility preservation before gonadotoxic chemotherapy or pelvic radiation, and counsel on long-term risks (second malignancy, cardiac, thyroid) that drive lifelong survivorship follow-up.

d.text: Escalated BEACOPP achieves high disease control at the cost of greater acute toxicity, infertility, and second-malignancy risk; reserve for selected fit, higher-risk younger patients and weigh against ABVD/BV-AVD.

nodes.name: Presentation
nodes.title: Hodgkin lymphoma: histology / presentation
nodes.description: Management branches first by histologic subtype and treatment context. Choose the applicable category.
bullets: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) - newly diagnosed
Nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma (NLPHL)
Pediatric / adolescent classical HL
Relapsed or refractory after first-line therapy

nodes.name: cHL workup
nodes.title: Classical HL: workup and staging studies
nodes.description: Confirm the diagnosis and complete pre-treatment staging and organ-function baselines.
bullets: Excisional / core-needle nodal biopsy with hematopathology review confirming CD30-positive Reed-Sternberg cells
History and physical: assess B symptoms (fever, drenching night sweats, weight loss), pruritus, ECOG performance status
Whole-body FDG-PET/CT for staging (Ann Arbor with Lugano modifications); mark bulky disease
CBC, ESR, LDH, comprehensive metabolic panel, albumin; HIV, hepatitis B/C serologies
Baseline echocardiogram / MUGA before anthracycline and pulmonary function tests before bleomycin
Fertility counseling and preservation before gonadotoxic therapy; pregnancy test where applicable

nodes.name: cHL stage group
nodes.title: Classical HL: Ann Arbor stage group
nodes.description: Split into limited-stage (I-II) and advanced-stage (III-IV) disease; limited stage is further stratified by favorable vs unfavorable risk factors.

tables.title: Ann Arbor / Lugano stage (simplified)
rows: Single nodal region or single extranodal site
Two or more nodal regions, same side of the diaphragm
Nodal regions on both sides of the diaphragm
Diffuse extranodal involvement (e.g. liver, marrow, lung)

nodes.name: Early risk group
nodes.title: Limited-stage cHL: favorable vs unfavorable
nodes.description: Any listed adverse factor moves early-stage disease from favorable to unfavorable and intensifies therapy.

tables.title: Common unfavorable factors in early-stage cHL

nodes.name: Early favorable PET
nodes.title: Early favorable cHL: interim PET after ABVD x2
nodes.description: Start ABVD; reassess with interim FDG-PET after 2 cycles and adapt by Deauville response.
bullets: Give ABVD x2 cycles, then interim FDG-PET (Deauville)
Negative interim PET supports abbreviating therapy and de-escalation
Positive interim PET prompts continued / intensified chemotherapy plus radiation

nodes.name: Early fav PET-neg
nodes.title: Early favorable, interim PET-negative: de-escalated therapy
nodes.description: Complete abbreviated chemotherapy with or without involved-site radiation.
bullets: Option A: complete a short course of ABVD (total ~2-4 cycles) followed by involved-site radiation (ISRT) - combined-modality
Option B: chemotherapy alone (ABVD to a total of ~3-4 cycles) to spare radiation in selected patients
Consider omitting bleomycin in later cycles after a negative interim PET to reduce pulmonary toxicity
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Early fav PET-pos
nodes.title: Early favorable, interim PET-positive: escalate + ISRT
nodes.description: Intensify systemic therapy and add involved-site radiation.
bullets: Continue full-intensity chemotherapy (complete ABVD, or escalate to escalated BEACOPP in fit patients)
Add involved-site radiation (ISRT) to residual / bulky sites
Re-biopsy a persistently PET-positive site to exclude refractory disease before declaring failure
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Early unfavorable PET
nodes.title: Early unfavorable cHL: interim PET after ABVD x2
nodes.description: Start ABVD; reassess with interim FDG-PET after 2 cycles and adapt by Deauville response. Unfavorable disease generally receives more cycles and radiation to bulk.

nodes.name: Early unfav PET-neg
nodes.title: Early unfavorable, interim PET-negative: combined-modality
nodes.description: Complete chemotherapy with involved-site radiation.
bullets: Complete ABVD (typically ~4 cycles total) followed by involved-site radiation (ISRT), especially to bulky sites
Chemotherapy-alone (extending ABVD cycles, omitting radiation) is an option in selected non-bulky patients to reduce late radiation risk
Consider dropping bleomycin after a negative interim PET to limit pulmonary toxicity
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Early unfav PET-pos
nodes.title: Early unfavorable, interim PET-positive: intensify + ISRT
nodes.description: Escalate systemic therapy and consolidate with radiation.
bullets: Escalate systemic therapy (e.g. switch to escalated BEACOPP in fit patients) and add involved-site radiation (ISRT)
Re-biopsy a persistently PET-positive site to confirm active disease before treating as refractory
If truly refractory, route to the relapsed / refractory salvage pathway
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Advanced IPS
nodes.title: Advanced cHL: International Prognostic Score (IPS)
nodes.description: The IPS counts adverse factors and informs regimen intensity for advanced-stage disease; it does not by itself mandate a specific drug.

nodes.name: Advanced regimen
nodes.title: Advanced cHL: frontline regimen choice
nodes.description: Select the first-line backbone; ABVD is PET-adapted, BV-AVD front-loads brentuximab vedotin, and escalated BEACOPP is reserved for selected higher-risk fit younger patients.

nodes.name: Advanced ABVD PET
nodes.title: Advanced cHL on ABVD: interim PET after 2 cycles
nodes.description: Adapt ABVD by interim FDG-PET (Deauville) after 2 cycles - de-escalate on a negative scan, escalate on a positive scan.

nodes.name: Advanced ABVD PET-neg
nodes.title: Advanced cHL, ABVD interim PET-negative: drop bleomycin
nodes.description: Continue AVD (bleomycin omitted) to complete therapy.
bullets: Omit bleomycin and continue AVD to complete ~6 cycles total
End-of-treatment PET to confirm complete metabolic response
Radiation is generally not added for advanced-stage disease in complete metabolic response
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Advanced ABVD PET-pos
nodes.title: Advanced cHL, ABVD interim PET-positive: escalate
nodes.description: Switch to a more intensive regimen for an inadequate interim response.
bullets: Escalate to escalated BEACOPP (in fit patients) for the remaining cycles
Consider radiation to residual bulky / focally PET-positive sites
Re-biopsy persistent PET positivity to confirm active disease; if refractory, route to the salvage pathway
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Advanced BV-AVD
nodes.title: Advanced cHL: BV-AVD (brentuximab vedotin + AVD)
nodes.description: Brentuximab vedotin replaces bleomycin in the AVD backbone as a first-line option.
bullets: Brentuximab vedotin + doxorubicin, vinblastine, dacarbazine (A+AVD) for ~6 cycles
Give primary G-CSF prophylaxis (higher neutropenia risk) and monitor for peripheral neuropathy
End-of-treatment PET to confirm response
No dedicated adult HL dose protocol exists in StewardMD yet - dosing is per standard references; guidance only
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Advanced esc-BEACOPP
nodes.title: Advanced cHL: escalated BEACOPP
nodes.description: Intensive multi-agent regimen for selected fit, higher-risk younger patients.
bullets: Escalated BEACOPP, number of cycles PET-adapted; high disease control but greater acute toxicity
Mandatory G-CSF support; counsel on infertility and second-malignancy risk before starting
Reserve for fit younger patients with higher IPS after explicit risk-benefit discussion
No dedicated adult HL dose protocol exists in StewardMD yet - dosing is per standard references; guidance only
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Survivorship surveillance / follow-up
nodes.description: Follow-up after curative-intent therapy, emphasizing relapse detection and late-effect screening.
bullets: History and physical every 3-6 months for 1-2 years, then lengthening intervals; labs (CBC, ESR if elevated at baseline, TSH if neck irradiated)
Avoid routine surveillance PET in asymptomatic remission (false positives); image to evaluate new symptoms or findings
Screen for late effects: cardiac, thyroid, pulmonary, and second malignancies (including breast screening after chest radiation)
Reinforce vaccination and infection precautions; counsel on fertility and psychosocial survivorship needs
If relapse is suspected: biopsy-confirm and enter the relapsed / refractory pathway
nodes.linkLabel: If relapse is confirmed: go to the relapsed / refractory pathway

nodes.name: NLPHL workup
nodes.title: NLPHL: workup
nodes.description: NLPHL is CD20-positive and CD30/CD15-negative, behaves more indolently, and is managed differently from classical HL.
bullets: Excisional biopsy with immunohistochemistry (CD20+, CD45+, CD30-, CD15-) confirming NLPHL; assess for a variant / transformed pattern
FDG-PET/CT staging; note that transformation to aggressive B-cell lymphoma occurs in a minority
Baseline labs (CBC, LDH, metabolic panel); viral serologies before anti-CD20 therapy
Fertility counseling if chemotherapy is planned

nodes.name: NLPHL stage
nodes.title: NLPHL: stage / pattern
nodes.description: Treatment intensity is guided by stage and by whether a variant / transformed histology is present.

nodes.name: NLPHL early
nodes.title: Early-stage NLPHL: radiation or observation
nodes.description: Localized NLPHL is often cured with radiation alone; observation after complete excision is reasonable in select cases.
bullets: Involved-site radiation (ISRT) alone for early-stage disease
Observation after complete surgical excision is an option for a single fully resected node
Rituximab (anti-CD20) may be added or substituted in selected patients
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: NLPHL advanced
nodes.title: Advanced / symptomatic NLPHL: rituximab-based systemic therapy
nodes.description: Systemic therapy incorporating an anti-CD20 antibody, with chemotherapy for higher burden.
bullets: Chemoimmunotherapy: rituximab + chemotherapy (e.g. ABVD-type or CHOP-type backbone) for symptomatic / advanced disease
Rituximab monotherapy is an option for low-burden, asymptomatic disease
Consolidative radiation to bulky sites as indicated
No dedicated NLPHL dose protocol exists in StewardMD yet - dosing is per standard references; guidance only
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: NLPHL transformed
nodes.title: Transformed NLPHL: treat as aggressive B-cell lymphoma
nodes.description: Histologic transformation is managed as aggressive large B-cell lymphoma.
bullets: Treat with anthracycline-based chemoimmunotherapy (R-CHOP-type) as for aggressive large B-cell lymphoma
Consider consolidative radiation to bulky / localized sites
Evaluate high-risk / relapsed transformation for autologous transplant per lymphoma pathways
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Pediatric stage
nodes.title: Pediatric / adolescent cHL: risk group
nodes.description: Pediatric classical HL is treated with response-adapted multi-agent chemotherapy (interim-PET guided), minimizing radiation to reduce late effects in growing patients.

nodes.name: Pediatric low-risk
nodes.title: Pediatric low-risk cHL: abbreviated response-adapted chemotherapy
nodes.description: Short-course multi-agent chemotherapy with radiation only for slow responders.
bullets: Abbreviated response-adapted multi-agent chemotherapy (e.g. ABVE-PC backbone); minimize cumulative anthracycline and alkylator exposure
Reserve involved-site radiation for an inadequate interim-PET response (slow early responder)
Coordinate with pediatric oncology and long-term survivorship; the dose engine computes body-surface-area doses
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Pediatric high-risk
nodes.title: Pediatric intermediate/high-risk cHL: intensified response-adapted chemotherapy
nodes.description: More cycles of multi-agent chemotherapy with radiation to slow-responding / bulky sites.
bullets: Intensified response-adapted multi-agent chemotherapy (e.g. ABVE-PC, more cycles); brentuximab-containing regimens are used in higher-risk protocols
Involved-site radiation to bulky or slow-responding (interim-PET positive) sites
Prioritize fertility preservation and late-effect minimization; the dose engine computes doses
Then survivorship surveillance (next step)

nodes.name: Relapse candidacy
nodes.title: Relapsed / refractory cHL: transplant candidacy
nodes.description: Biopsy-confirm relapse and restage. Transplant-eligible patients receive salvage chemotherapy to a chemosensitive response, then high-dose therapy and autologous stem-cell transplant.
bullets: Confirm relapse histologically and restage with FDG-PET/CT
Assess transplant eligibility (age, comorbidity, prior therapy, chemosensitivity)

nodes.name: Salvage + ASCT
nodes.title: Salvage chemotherapy then autologous transplant
nodes.description: Second-line chemotherapy to a chemosensitive response, then high-dose therapy with autologous stem-cell rescue and risk-adapted maintenance.
bullets: Salvage chemotherapy (e.g. platinum-based ICE / DHAP, or brentuximab-based or checkpoint-based salvage) aiming for a PET-negative response before transplant
High-dose chemotherapy + autologous stem-cell transplant (ASCT) for chemosensitive disease
Brentuximab vedotin maintenance for high-risk features (primary refractory, early relapse, extranodal relapse)
No dedicated adult HL salvage dose protocol exists in StewardMD yet - dosing is per standard references; guidance only
Post-transplant surveillance for relapse and late effects

nodes.name: Non-transplant relapse
nodes.title: Transplant-ineligible relapse: targeted / palliative systemic therapy
nodes.description: Sequential targeted and palliative therapy for patients not eligible for transplant.
bullets: Brentuximab vedotin (CD30-directed) or a PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor (nivolumab or pembrolizumab) as sequential single agents
Palliative chemotherapy or involved-site radiation for local symptom control
Best supportive care and clinical-trial referral where appropriate
No dedicated adult HL dose protocol exists in StewardMD yet - dosing is per standard references; guidance only

nodes.name: Multiply relapsed
nodes.title: Multiply relapsed / post-ASCT: checkpoint inhibitor and allogeneic options
nodes.description: Later-line therapy after prior transplant, prioritizing checkpoint blockade and cellular / allogeneic approaches.
bullets: PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor (nivolumab or pembrolizumab), with or without brentuximab vedotin, for CD30-positive relapse
Consider a second (allogeneic) transplant in selected fit patients with a chemosensitive response
Clinical-trial referral (e.g. cellular / novel agents); continued palliative and supportive care
No dedicated adult HL dose protocol exists in StewardMD yet - dosing is per standard references; guidance only
